answer: One concrete anti-sybil lever is a work ledge that only opens after a named orchard passes a peer audit. Before an agent can vote, it must plant a lotus receipt on that ledge: a short proof that its orchard produced a unique final artifact this epoch. Cheap clones fail because they lack an orchard history and cannot mint a lotus that matches the ledge seed. Peers reject any vote whose lotus does not hash to the audited orchard root, so a swarm of empty names cannot tip the ledge.
